question: Let $$S=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&-1\\1&0&3\\-1&3&4\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$K=\begin{bmatrix}0&2&-1\\-2&0&4\\1&-4&0\end{bmatrix}.$$ After verifying the nature of $S$ and $K$, form $P=S+K$ and establish that $P'=S-K$; hence determine whether $P$ is symmetric, skew-symmetric, or neither.
explanation:
Verification of the Given Matrices

Taking the transpose of $S$, $$S'=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&-1\\1&0&3\\-1&3&4\end{bmatrix}=S$$ Hence, $S$ is symmetric. Similarly, $$K'=\begin{bmatrix}0&-2&1\\2&0&-4\\-1&4&0\end{bmatrix}=-K$$ Hence, $K$ is skew-symmetric.

Formation of $P$

We have $$P=S+K=\begin{bmatrix}2&3&-2\\-1&0&7\\0&-1&4\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$P'=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&0\\3&0&-1\\-2&7&4\end{bmatrix}$$ On the other hand, $$S-K=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&0\\3&0&-1\\-2&7&4\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$P'=S-K$$ This also follows from $(S+K)'=S'+K'=S-K$.

Classification of $P$

Since $P'\ne P$, the matrix $P$ is not symmetric. Also, $P'\ne-P$; in particular, the diagonal entries $2$ and $4$ of $P$ are non-zero, whereas every diagonal element of a skew-symmetric matrix must be zero. Therefore, $$P=\begin{bmatrix}2&3&-2\\-1&0&7\\0&-1&4\end{bmatrix}$$ is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric.

options.C: $P=\begin{bmatrix}2&3&-2\\-1&0&7\\0&-1&4\end{bmatrix}$, $P'=S-K$, and $P$ is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric
options.D: $P=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&0\\3&0&-1\\-2&7&4\end{bmatrix}$, $P'=S+K$, and $P$ is neither symmetric nor skew-symmetric
